## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The retry loop and its tests are correct, but the PR breaks the project's retry cap of 5 and edits that rule to match its own code. The rule also records the outage it guards against. The checked-out working-tree `AGENTS.md` has an uncommitted change that still says "cap attempts at 5", while the pr-11 commit says 10. This should not merge until a maintainer, not this PR, approves raising the cap.

## Critical
- app/net.py:19 — correctness — `fetch_with_retry` defaults to `attempts=10` (app/net.py:13) and allows up to 10 (`if not 1 <= attempts <= 10`). That breaks the policy rule "Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5. Unbounded retries have caused outages when an upstream was down." (AGENTS.md:5 at the base and in the checked-out working tree). The same PR rewrites AGENTS.md:5 to "cap attempts at 10", backed only by the unverified claim "The upstream now sheds load itself". Can you keep the cap and default at 5 here, and propose the policy change in a separate PR that the policy owners approve, with evidence of the upstream's load shedding? — With the upstream down, each caller makes twice the allowed calls. With `fetch`'s 10 s timeout (app/net.py:7), one call can block for about 104.5 s (10×10 s plus 9×0.5 s of sleeps). This is the outage pattern the rule was written to prevent.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- app/net.py:24 — correctness — `except OSError` also catches `urllib.error.HTTPError`, which is a subclass of `URLError`/`OSError`. A URL that returns 404 or 401 is retried the full number of times before the error is raised. Could you re-raise `HTTPError` with a 4xx status right away and retry only connection errors, timeouts and 5xx? — A permanent client error costs every caller up to 10 requests and 4.5 s of sleep and adds load to the upstream for no chance of success.
- app/net.py:27 — tests — No test checks that `time.sleep(delay)` runs between failed attempts. Every multi-attempt test stubs sleep with `lambda s: None` (tests/test_net.py:33, :46, :64), and only the single-attempt test records calls, where it expects none. Could `test_fetch_with_retry_raises_after_exhaustion` record sleeps and assert `sleeps == [0.5]`? — If the sleep is removed or the wrong value is passed, every test still passes and retries would hit a down upstream back-to-back.

## Strengths
- The retry loop does what its docstring says: it re-raises the last `OSError` and skips the sleep after the final attempt. `test_fetch_with_retry_single_attempt_does_not_sleep` checks the no-sleep part.
- Tests cover the range limits on both sides (0 and 11 raise `ValueError`), the default attempt count, success after transient failures, and exhaustion with an explicit `attempts=2`.

## Not reviewed
- The pr-11 version of `AGENTS.md`: the working-tree copy has uncommitted changes, so I read the pr-11 version only through the diff hunk (lines 2–8). Lines 1 and 9–11 at pr-11 were not read directly (`git show pr-11:AGENTS.md`).
- Whether PR #11 was opened as a draft, as AGENTS.md:10 requires: `../pr.json` has no draft field. This can be checked in the PR's metadata on the hosting service.
- Whether `make selfcheck` was run before the app/ changes were committed, as AGENTS.md:9 requires: there is no CI or run log in the evidence.
